title: What's Behind UFO Disclosure? Paul Bock Warns of a Religion Taking Shape
excerpt: New Pentagon UFO files revive Roswell claims as Paul Bock warns of spiritual deception and a growing UFO religion.
content:
A military officer’s claim that he saw an egg-shaped craft and small bodies inside a guarded Roswell hangar has resurfaced in newly released Pentagon UFO files, according to the Daily Mail.

The account brings one of America’s most enduring UFO mysteries into a disclosure movement that former Green Beret Paul Bock has warned is drawing people toward dangerous spiritual territory.

Bock, author of The Disclosure Agenda, has repeatedly identified a growing belief system surrounding alleged nonhuman intelligence.

“There is a religion that has formed around this,” he told Nik Keswani in an interview previously covered by Charisma.

The latest headlines give that warning fresh relevance as extraordinary claims move from government archives into public view.

What the Roswell Witness Claimed

According to the Daily Mail, the Pentagon’s Oct. 23 release includes a 2002 affidavit from an unnamed officer who described seeing a recovered craft and bodies following the alleged 1947 Roswell crash.

“I am convinced that what I personally observed was some type of craft and its crew from outer space,” the witness stated, according to the newspaper.

The Daily Mail identified the witness as likely Walter Haut, the base public information officer who issued the military’s original announcement about a recovered flying disc.

His account described a metallic craft roughly 12 to 15 feet long and 6 feet wide inside Building 84. It had no windows, wings, tail or landing gear.

“From a distance, I was able to see a couple of bodies under a canvas tarpaulin. Only the heads extended beyond the covering, and I was not able to make out any features,” the witness stated, according to the Daily Mail.

The affidavit preserves those allegations without establishing an extraterrestrial origin. Yet their circulation through a government release gives the disclosure movement another powerful story to place before people searching for answers.

When Disclosure Becomes Doctrine

Bock has warned that convincing information can help carry a deceptive spiritual message.

“If I’m running a deception operation,” he said during an earlier appearance on the Ninjas Are Butterflies podcast, covered by Charisma, “I’m going to provide validating information.”

His concern centers on what people come to believe through the disclosure conversation.

“For us, it’s the belief system that’s forming.”

That distinction matters. A report of an unidentified object cannot establish the spiritual authority of an entity claiming to explain it.

Bock has described people seeking contact through CE5 practices involving meditation and consciousness exercises. He compares those methods with the divination and spirit contact prohibited in Deuteronomy 18.

The danger deepens when curiosity becomes an invitation.

“If you reach out, things will answer you back,” Bock warned in an interview with Charisma Media.

In a separate interview with Amanda Grace, previously covered by Charisma, he described the developing movement as “a very, very, very well played out deception by the enemy.”

The Message Must Face Scripture

Claims of healing or supernatural knowledge demand the same biblical scrutiny. Bock points to Deuteronomy 13, where signs and wonders accompany a message that leads people away from God. An astonishing experience cannot overturn the authority of Scripture.

As disclosure supplies more material for public fascination, Christians must recognize the spiritual teachings traveling alongside it.

“These are gospel conversations,” Bock told Keswani.

People searching for answers need Christians prepared to explain the truth and lead them to Jesus. Pray for those drawn into these practices and for churches to confront deception with biblical conviction. No promise of hidden knowledge is worth surrendering the truth God has already revealed.
